headline: Small craft advisory outside; no real break, work the west corner
body:
Small craft advisory is up through late Sunday night for the outer waters — Santa Rosa, Osborn and San Nicolas all sit under it, with 15–25 kt NW and 6–9 ft seas, and SW to SE swell from Hurricanes Odalys and Polo is building into next week. The east channel is clean by comparison: today light, going SW 10–15 in the afternoon, 2–3 ft inshore and 3.5 ft at the triangle's middle. Sunday brings patchy morning fog, 3.8 ft, and W 10–20 by afternoon.

Saturday is the day, and go early. The catch is temperature: the triangle corners read 71.2 west, 71.4 south, 72.6 east today, so the 64–68 band is nowhere inside the zone — start at the west corner south of Santa Cruz, the coolest water on the chart's near ground, and let bait decide the rest. The far runs are warmer still, 73.1 at Osborn and 73.2 at San Nicolas; not better water, not worth the fuel under an advisory. Santa Rosa's 69.5 Sunday comes with 18–20 kt and 6.1 ft. Pass.
